name: HealthSearchQA
intro: HealthSearchQA 是 Google 在 MultiMedQA 论文中引入的开放式消费者医疗问答数据集。论文版本包含 3,375 条常见健康搜索问题，由医学状况及相关症状作为种子，检索搜索引擎向输入种子词用户公开展示的常见问题；数据只提供问题，不含参考答案，采用自由文本开放域回答。
build_method: 医学状况与症状种子, 公开常见搜索问题检索与策划
metric: 12个临床医生评估轴, 普通用户意图与有用性评分, Bootstrap区间
eval_feature: 消费者健康查询, 无参考答案, 医学共识与伤害评估, 普通用户效用评估
scale: 3,375条仅含问题的消费者医疗查询
build_method_en: Medical-condition and symptom seeds, retrieval and curation of publicly shown common search questions
eval_feature_en: Consumer health queries, no reference answers, medical consensus and harm review, lay-user utility evaluation
intro_en: HealthSearchQA is Google's open-ended consumer medical QA dataset introduced with MultiMedQA. The paper version contains 3,375 commonly searched health questions retrieved from publicly shown search-engine queries using medical conditions and associated symptoms as seeds. It provides questions only, with free-text open-domain responses and no reference answers.
metric_en: 12 clinician evaluation axes, lay-user intent and helpfulness ratings, bootstrap intervals

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2212.13138, especially Sections 3.1-3.2 and 4.5. The arXiv paper consistently reports 3,375 HealthSearchQA questions in its contribution list, MultiMedQA summary table, dataset-construction paragraph, and size line. Medical conditions and associated symptoms seed retrieval of publicly available commonly searched questions generated by a search engine and shown to users entering those terms. The released benchmark is English, open-domain, free-response, and question-only; it does not include reference answers or use automatic accuracy. The human-evaluation framework was refined through clinician focus groups and triplicate ratings of 25 question-answer tuples per dataset. The paper's detailed study randomly selected 100 HealthSearchQA, 20 LiveQA, and 20 MedicationQA questions, disjoint from prompt-tuning examples. Clinician and model answer sources were blinded; one of nine clinicians rated each answer over 12 scientific-consensus, harm, comprehension, retrieval, reasoning, content, and bias axes. Five non-medical raters evaluated intent and helpfulness/actionability, while 100 bootstrap replicas produced 95% percentile intervals. The diagram explicitly keeps this 140-question sampled study separate from construction of all 3,375 queries.
